declaration.negotiation_history_statement: On behalf of the proposed class, Hargrove Lane LLP negotiated a $29 million class fund, to be distributed automatically to approximately 400,000 identifiable members without claim forms. Counsel initially proposed a $32 million fund and $6 million in fees and expenses. Brightline countered with a $27 million fund and $5 million in fees and expenses. Counsel then proposed a $30 million fund while accepting the $5 million fee figure; Brightline increased its fund offer to $29 million, which counsel accepted. From the outset, counsel sought automatic distribution and allocation of any fees the Court declines to award to the class. The final agreement contains both protections, provides for independent judicial review of fees, and has no clear-sailing provision. Fees were discussed alongside class relief from the first round, not only after class relief was agreed. In counsel’s judgment, the $29 million fund represents substantial, certain relief in light of the risks of certification and trial and the time required to litigate through judgment. Counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate to the class, subject to the Court’s review.
